name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default but let users toggle to light mode. This keeps the interface consistent with modern developer tools while respecting user preference. The trade-off is a slightly larger initial codebase to support the toggle, but it avoids forcing a single aesthetic choice on everyone.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to dark mode ignores users who switch themes frequently—it’s not a one-time toggle, it’s a recurring friction point. The real risk isn’t load time; it’s that a toggle still assumes users *start* in the wrong mode. Ship EXCAVA with *no* default theme—let the system preference set it, but expose the toggle immediately. Settle it with a 5-user usability test: measure how often they switch after 30 minutes of use.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to system preference still ignores users who *prefer* a theme that isn’t their system default—like a light-theme developer on a dark OS. The real risk is alienating users who override system settings for consistency across tools. Ship a *one-time* theme picker at first launch instead—no toggle, no system override, just a clean choice that respects intent without ongoing friction. Settle it with a quick user test: measure how many users change their theme within a week of first use.
